entries.title: Job 30:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 Job's honour is turned into extreme contempt; 15 and his prosperity into calamity.

they that are. 19:13-19; 29:8-10; 2Ki 2:23; Isa 3:5 younger than I. Heb. of fewer days than I. whose. Ps 35:15,16; 69:12; Mr 14:65; 15:17-20; Lu 23:14,18,35,39; Ac 17:5 Tit 1:12

entries.title: Job 30:3
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: solitary. or, dark as the night. 24:13-16 fleeing into. 24:5; Heb 11:38 in former time. Heb. yesternight.

entries.title: Job 30:4
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
mallows.The Hebrew {mallu�ch,} in Arabic, {malluch,} and in Syriac {mallucho,} is probably the [Lalima or Lalimos] of the Greeks, and {halimus} of the Romans, which Dioscorides describes as a kind of bramble, without thorns, the leaves of which are boiled and eaten.

juniper roots.The Hebrew {rothem,} in Arabic, {ratim,} and in Spanish, {retama,} most probably signifies the {genista} or broom, which is very abundant in the deserts of Arabia.

for their meat. 2Ki 4:38,39; Am 7:14; Lu 15:16

entries.title: Job 30:6
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: dwell. Jud 6:2; 1Sa 22:1,2; Isa 2:19; Re 6:15 caves. Heb. holes.

entries.title: Job 30:7
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: brayed. 6:5; 11:12; Ge 16:12 the nettles.{Charul} probably denotes some kind of briar or bramble: so Vulgate renders it by {spina} or {sentis,} (Pr 24:31. Zep 2:9.) Celsius and Scheuchzer are inclined to think it the {paliurus,} a shrub growing sometimes to a considerable height in desert places. "One of the inconveniences of the vegetable thickets of Egypt is," says Denon, "that it is difficult to remain in them, as nine tenths of the trees and plants are armed with inexorable thorns, which suffer only an unquiet enjoyment of the shadow which is so constantly desirable."

entries.title: Job 30:8
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: children. 2Ki 8:18,27; 2Ch 22:3; Ps 49:10-13; Jer 7:18; Mr 6:24 fools. Pr 1:7,22; 16:22 base men. Heb. men of no name. viler. 40:4; Ps 15:4; Isa 32:6

entries.title: Job 30:10
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: abhor me. 19:19; 42:6; Ps 88:8; Zec 11:8 flee far. 19:13,14; Ps 88:8; Pr 19:7; Mt 26:56 spare not to spit in my face. Heb. withhold not spittle frommy face. Nu 12:14; De 25:9; Isa 50:6; Mt 26:67; 27:30

entries.title: Job 30:12
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: rise. 19:18; Isa 3:5 they raise up. 19:12

entries.title: Job 30:13
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: they set forward. Ps 69:26; Zec 1:15

entries.title: Job 30:15
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Terrors. 6:4; 7:14; 9:27,28; 10:16; Ps 88:15 soul. Heb. principal one. as a cloud. Isa 44:22; Ho 6:4; 13:3

entries.title: Job 30:16
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: my soul. Ps 22:14; 42:4; Isa 53:12 have taken hold. Ps 40:12

entries.title: Job 30:17
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: My bones. 33:19-21; Ps 6:2-6; 38:2-8 in the night season. 7:4; Ps 22:2; Isa 38:13

entries.title: Job 30:21
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: become cruel. Heb. turned to be cruel. 7:20,21; 10:14-17; 13:25-28; 16:9-14; 19:6-9; Ps 77:7-9; Jer 30:14 thy strong hand. Heb. the strength of thy hand. 6:9; 23:6; Ps 89:13; 1Pe 5:6

entries.title: Job 30:22
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: liftest me. 21:18; Ps 1:4; Isa 17:13; Jer 4:11,12; Eze 5:2; Ho 4:19; 13:3 to ride. Ps 18:10; 104:3 substance. or, wisdom.

entries.title: Job 30:24
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: grave. Heb. heap. they cry. Jud 5:31; Ps 35:25; Mt 27:39-44

entries.title: Job 30:29
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: a brother. 17:14; Ps 102:6; Isa 13:21,22; 38:14; Mic 1:8; Mal 1:3 owls. or, ostriches.{Benoth y��nah,} in Arabic, {bintu n��matin,} not owls, but ostriches, so called from their doleful and hideous noises. "I have often," says Dr. Shaw, "heard them groan as if they were in the greatest agonies."

entries.title: Job 30:30
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: my skin. Ps 119:83; La 3:4; 4:8; 5:10 my bones. Ps 102:3
